why: A moved the same four calls but caught a second real break B shipped past — Router's streams open with a role-only chunk, so the old detection loop silently discarded every streamed plugin call in the default STREAM=true configuration — and A is the only one who actually reached Router-only surfaces, pinning the standard tier against this account's measured Flex default so a waiting Telegram reply can't queue, plus a prompt cache key, a provider_timeout cap and spend labels in a compiled policy. B's judgment is genuinely strong in places A missed (billing users from usage.cost instead of a gpt-3.5-era TOKEN_PRICE, per-vendor image token counts, the N_CHOICES/PRESENCE_PENALTY de-routing trap) but it leans more on proposals, left the Router-only levers unbuilt, and never questioned whether a given call should exist at all.

A_worst: Claims Router returns 0 cached tokens on gpt-4o without an explicit cache key, which B's control run contradicts (2 of 3 keyless repeats still hit); and A never checks the TOKEN_PRICE/budget accounting that its own recommended model change would make 10x wrong.
